quote: carried out an evaluation of
why: The action is buried in a noun; "worked out" or "evaluated" says it directly.

quote: had come to the realization that
why: "Had realized" says the same with the verb restored.

quote: My insurance renewal
why: "Renewal" names a document that arrived, not an action the writer performed.

quote: a new transmission
why: "Transmission" names a car part.

quote: The decision to sell was made in April
why: The passive hides that the writer decided, in an essay about the writer's own choice.

quote: The combination was forgotten twice
why: The writer forgot it; the passive removes the only possible actor.

quote: My bike was stolen in June.
why: The thief is unknown and irrelevant, so the passive is the right choice.

quote: are cleared by city crews
why: The actor is stated in the by-phrase.

quote: I left the house at six-forty. I reached the bottom of the hill by seven. I arrived
why: Three consecutive sentences open with "I" and the same subject-verb shape.

quote: After eleven years of sitting in morning traffic behind a school bus, I
why: Twelve words of introductory phrase come before the subject.

quote: It should be noted that
why: The phrase announces a statement instead of making it.

quote: was very hard
why: "Very" intensifies without adding information.

quote: I actually prefer it
why: "Actually" marks no contrast here and can go.

quote: basically forgotten
why: "Basically" hedges a plain statement.

quote: I can only describe
why: "Only" limits the claim and carries meaning.

quote: I have never once been late
why: "Never once" states the claim exactly; it is not emphasis for effect.

quote: picturesque row of Victorian houses on Linden Street, then the picturesque
why: An uncommon adjective appears twice in one sentence for no reason.

quote: plain and simple
why: A stock doubled pair where neither word adds to the other.

quote: followed the bus routes instead
why: "Bus routes" repeats because it names the same thing as the previous sentence.

quote: a warm cocoon, an anchor that kept me moored
why: Two figures contradict each other and neither says what the car did.

quote: the city opened up like a book
why: Stock imagery stands in for saying what the writer noticed.

quote: is a bottleneck at rush hour
why: A dead metaphor used literally for a narrow bridge that holds up traffic.

quote: By the time I reached the top of the hill that February
why: The paragraph refers to the hill and the first winter before the reader learns about either; it belongs after the winter paragraph.

quote: Municipal snow contracts in our city specify
why: The sentence opens with new material unconnected to the wet commute the previous sentence described.

quote: Everyone's situation is different, and what works for one person will not necessarily work for another.
why: The whole paragraph is throat-clearing and restatement that the essay does not need.
